messages.subject: MATLABSTAN
parts:
Hi everybody,
I am new to Stan and have a biological model to estimate its unknown parameters.
My model is

dx/dt= beta* p(t)/(p(t)+theta)-alpha *x(t)
where

p(t)=(h0+(1-h0)./(1+exp(-b1*(t-t1)))).*(h2+(1-h2)./(1+exp(b2*(t-t2))));

In the model the parameters beta, h0, h2, t1, b1, b2, theta and alpha are unknown.

I have measured x(t) under tow conditions and for each condition I have three replicates.So, I have 

overall 6 sets of data for condition 1: x11, x12, x13 and condition2, x21, x22 and x23.  I plan to compare the parameters alpha, beta and theta at two different conditions to see if there  is any change. I do not know if I can model measurement error as noise.  I would highly appreciate if you could introduce me a similar example in MatlabStan (I do not know R) .

Thanks

Bita

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] MATLABSTAN
parts:
The Stan modeling language, where you specify the model,
is shared across all interfaces. It just specifies
the data, parameters, and log density (or penalized max
liklelihood) you're trying to fit.

I'm not sure why you're defining a derivative and how that
relates to the log density you want to define in a Stan program.

- Bob
